texts: A young woman newly found to have Marfan syndrome (a mutation at 15q21, the fibrillin-1 gene) needs imaging of the whole aorta, and a CT scan is the best next step here.
Marfan disease affects the entire aorta, so a baseline CT (or MRI) of the chest and abdomen measures the root, the ascending aorta and the rest, and finds any silent dilation or dissection.
Echocardiography sees the root and the valve but not the whole aorta.
A carotid duplex, a chest X-ray or pulmonary function tests do not answer the aortic question.
In the picture, the cat slices the whole orca from arch to tail and Chopper puts the slices on the first page of the album.
Memory hook: a new Marfan: slice the whole orca once.
